newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BP option features in quiet UK trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BP option features in quiet UK trade.

text.p: The UK traded options market was on standby at midday as dealers awaited key U.S. unemployment figures, due at 1330 GMT.
The U.S. December jobless figures, including average hourly earnings and non-farm payroll total may give the market clues as to the likelihood of a near-term U.S. rate hike, dealers said.
"It's been fairly quiet this morning. We're all waiting on the U.S. numbers," one dealer said.
A synthetic long position in British Petroleum was established when one dealer sold 1,000 BP April 650 puts at 10p and then bought 1,000 April 750 calls at 18p.
This strategy is equivalent to owning the stock and is bullishly oriented, since the greatest profit will occur if the share increases in price.

If the underlying BP stock rises far enough, profits can be generated on both the long call and the short put. If the stock remains relatively stable, the call purchase will be a loss, but the put sale will be in profit.
The risk occurs if the underlyling share drops in price, producing losses on both the short put and the long call.
BP shares were up 4p at 701-1/2p, against the weaker market trend. The FTSE 100 index was down 17.6 at 4,069.4 by 1255 GMT.
